title: UK pledges £120M more for AI Security Institute and £100M AI Biosecurity Lab
summary: HM Treasury set out a pre-Budget AI package of over £600 million, including an extra £120 million for the AI Security Institute and £165 million for a National AI Biosecurity Initiative. Its £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab is backed by up to £200 million in model credits from OpenAI and Anthropic.
reason: Government money for frontier-model testing raises oversight capacity (F3 up); AI-driven bio-threat detection lowers catastrophic risk (F8 down). Formal sign-off comes in Wednesday's Budget, so it is a signal for now.

title: Texas sues OpenAI and Altman, seeks court evaluator approval for new models
summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a 67-page suit in Collin County under the state's deceptive trade practices and child online safety laws. It asks the court to block ChatGPT for minors in Texas and require a court-appointed evaluator to approve new models.
reason: A ninth state suit adds to the legal pushback against OpenAI (F9 up); the requested pre-release model review would add outside oversight (F3 up). Follows the eight-state suits scored on 16 Oct.

title: China's Nanbeige releases open-weight 33B agent model under Apache 2.0
summary: Nanbeige, the AI lab of recruitment platform BOSS Zhipin, published Nanbeige4.3-33B on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, aimed at agentic coding and office tasks. Its benchmark wins over similar-size open models are self-reported.
reason: Another capable open-weight model spreads agent capability more widely (F5 down) and adds a small step in capability (F1 up); benchmarks are the lab's own.
